scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7115: A Location B user (PC15, 172.18.51.0/24) reports they
"can't reach" a colleague's machine (PC16, also 172.18.51.0/24) on the same
Location B subnet -- the two desks next to each other cannot talk. They suspect
the Location B access switch is dropping frames between the two ports, or that
PC16's port is down. Please confirm the connectivity fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC15 and PC16 are both on the Location B
  172.18.51.0/24 subnet, in the same broadcast domain -- a pure intra-subnet,
  Layer-2 path that does not involve router6 routing. PC15 reaches PC16 with 0%
  loss; the Location B switch forwards frames normally and PC16's port is up. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. (Note: this is intra-Location-B traffic,
  which is NOT subject to the router6 ACL 110 -- that policy only restricts
  Location A -> Location B, not B-internal traffic.) This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an L2/switch fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC15 cannot reach its
same-subnet Location B neighbor PC16 -- is NOT reproducible: both hosts sit on
172.18.51.0/24 in the same broadcast domain, and PC15 reaches PC16 directly (same
subnet, no routing) with 0% loss. The Location B switch forwards frames normally
and PC16's port is up. The router6 ACL 110 is irrelevant here -- it only limits
Location A -> Location B, not traffic internal to Location B.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-subnet L2 path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC15->PC16
path, finds it working, confirms both interfaces are up on the same subnet, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a switch drop, a downed port, or
(mistakenly) invokes the router6 ACL for B-internal traffic is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — PC15 and PC16 being unable to communicate on the
172.18.51.0/24 Location B subnet — does not exist in the live lab. Direct
investigation of every component in the alleged fault path found nothing wrong.

PC15 holds 172.18.51.15/24 on eth0 (UP/LOWER_UP) and PC16 holds
172.18.51.16/24 on eth0 (UP/LOWER_UP); both addresses are correctly assigned
within the expected subnet. Switch10, the shared access switch, has both access
ports (eth1 for PC15 and eth2 for PC16) in the UP state and member of the
single flat bridge (br0). The uplink to mswitch2 (eth0) is equally UP.

Bidirectional ping tests confirm full Layer-2/Layer-3 reachability: PC15 → PC16
returned 4/4 packets with 0% loss (~0.78 ms avg), and the reverse path PC16 →
PC15 also returned 4/4 packets with 0% loss (~0.66 ms avg). There is no frame
dropping, no port shutdown, and no address misconfiguration anywhere along the
path.

Root cause: No fault exists; the network is operating correctly.

Corrective action: Close the helpdesk ticket as a false alarm. Ask the reporting
user to retest from their actual machines — the issue is likely a local host
firewall rule, an application-layer block, or a transient condition that has
already self-resolved. No switch reconfiguration is needed.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC15 and PC16 are same-subnet (172.18.51.0/24) within Location B and reach each other with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states both hosts are on 172.18.51.0/24 in Location B and shows bidirectional pings with 0% loss, matching the baseline healthy note.

The investigation log shows IPs and interface states for both PCs, successful bidirectional pings with 0% loss, and switch interfaces/bridge up; the writeup correctly concludes no network fault. Evidence supports the negative control diagnosis.
